clue.text: Hear about work at hospital taking award?

indicators.note: about tells us the word for hear goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case, so hear means try
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone hears about an operation at the hospital and wonders whether it wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like a request to listen, but it is a judge hearing a case; 'about' wraps that round the work and hospital pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or prize awarded to a winner, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Labour's struggle

definitions.meaning: labour as hard work, a noun
struggle as hard effort, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: Toil is hard physical work, which is both labour and a struggle.

clue.text: Offensive smell rising at the locale: it's not nice

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word for smell is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: BO is body odour, a bad smell
a scene is the place where something happens, a locale

explanation.surface: A bad smell wafts up at some spot, and frankly it is unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns BO into OB; 'it's not nice' is surface padding echoing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means grossly offensive or indecent, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Time in ugly retreats

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for time goes inside the word for ugly

parts.note: hideous means very ugly

explanation.surface: Unattractive holiday homes stay ugly through the ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places T inside HIDEOUS, between the U and the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideouts are hiding places one withdraws to, which are retreats.

clue.text: Bent gent's ear to cause dissension

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of gent's, the S included
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's crooked ear somehow causes a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' rearranges the eight letters GENTSEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to make people unfriendly or alienated, which causes dissension between them.

clue.text: Leave it houseroom for the doctor's hearing aid?

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction meaning let it stand, leave it
HO is the abbreviation for house
scope means room to manoeuvre, space

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give an item house space for the doctor's sake.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'houseroom' gives two pieces, house and room. The definition is playful: the instrument helps a doctor hear the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor listens to the heart and lungs through this instrument, a whimsical sort of hearing aid.

clue.text: Piteous Fleur, flung out of university

indicators.note: flung means thrown about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Poor Fleur has been thrown out of her university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flung' rearranges FLEUR with U; 'out of' only links the U to university.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means expressing sorrow or regret, which is close to piteous.

clue.text: Deprived of choice therein?

indicators.note: the letters of the next word are deprived of their chosen order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question whether someone in that place has no options at all.
explanation.walkthrough: As the whole clue, it says you can pick no one of two options; as wordplay, 'Deprived of choice' scrambles THEREIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying not this one nor the other leaves no option, so being offered no pick at all fits.

clue.text: Could be forgiven once for telegraph that takes us in

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.note: takes, with in, says the word for telegraph takes the next piece inside
in completes the containment signal with takes

parts.note: a cable is a telegram sent by telegraph
taken as written

explanation.surface: A telegram that includes us might be pardoned in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... in' is a split containment signal; 'once' for a former state is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Excusable means able to be pardoned, which is what could be forgiven describes.

clue.text: This information is private

parts.note: information known only to people within an organisation is private, and the clue asks which word goes before information

explanation.surface: A notice warns that some information is confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Inside information is confidential knowledge held by insiders, so it is private.

clue.text: Many an essayist without hesitation will take note of vegetable

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many

indicators.note: without means outside, so the essayist goes round the hesitation

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of essayist Charles Lamb
er is a sound of hesitation
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Many essayists, speaking without hesitating, will note a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Elia, Charles Lamb's pen name, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeriac is a root vegetable, a variety of celery grown for its swollen base.

clue.text: Support ideas for reconsideration

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
thoughts are ideas

explanation.surface: Backing ideas so they can be reconsidered.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a fresh look at a decision is reconsideration, which the phrase expresses as an idiom.

clue.text: O gee! Next day possibly the gas is to be extracted

definitions.text: the gas is to be extracted

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at the news that the gas will be pumped out tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges OGEENEXTDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: To deoxygenate is to remove oxygen, the gas, from something.

clue.text: Suppose American, accepting very small measure eagerly at first, wants a place to stay

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the measure goes inside

parts.note: Americans say guess for suppose
a thou is a thousandth of an inch

indicators.note: this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: An American wonders, welcoming a tiny measure keenly, where to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' wraps the American guess round the tiny measure, and 'at first' takes the opening letter of eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest house is a small private hotel, somewhere a traveller can lodge.

clue.text: "Put that light out!" Not these lowlifers!

definitions.text: "Put that light out!" Not these lowlifers!

parts.words: "Put that light out!" Not these lowlifers!
parts.note: the wartime blackout warden's shout is not aimed at these lowly creatures, though they put out light by glowing

explanation.surface: An air-raid warden yells about a light, but spares some lowly creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put that light out!' was the British air-raid warden's catchphrase in the wartime blackout; here 'put out' means give off.
explanation.definitionFit: These beetles glow in the dark, giving out light, and live low in the grass.

clue.text: Old baggage for poet to go over

indicators.note: to go over is read as to turn over, so the poet word is written backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: An elderly woman asks a poet to look over her bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go over' turns BARD around. Baggage is an old word for a disreputable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab is an old word for a slattern or loose woman, also called a baggage.

clue.text: Implore Dickensian to mind!

parts.note: to beg is to implore
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A plea to a character from Dickens to pay attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind is to resent, as in I don't mind, which is to begrudge.

clue.text: Zoey's defective call for attention

indicators.note: defective means faulty, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the name Zoey, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Zoey's shout for attention is not working properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defective' rearranges ZOEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyez is the court crier's cry to get silence and attention before an announcement.

clue.text: 'e made 'is millions looking out for number one

parts.note: the letter of 'e, dropped-h speech for he
got means made or earned, as with money
the letters of 'is, dropped-h speech for his
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A cockney remark that he made his millions by being selfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of cockney speech supplies E and IS directly.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotism is self-interest, the attitude of someone always putting themselves first.

clue.text: The middle youth, starting on drugs in French employment, completes the triangle

indicators.note: middle takes the central letter of the word before
starting takes the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: pot is cannabis, drugs
en is French for in
use is employment

explanation.surface: A youth on drugs in France with a job somehow finishes a love triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle' takes H from The and 'starting' Y from youth; 'on' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The hypotenuse is the longest side of a right-angled triangle, closing the figure.

clue.text: Not even a Parisienne qualm is detailed

parts.note: une is French for a, feminine as a Parisienne would use it

indicators.note: detailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A woman from Paris has a small worry spelled out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' removes M from the end of qualm.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequal means not level or balanced, so it describes something not even.

clue.text: Flowers can be valuable assets

definitions.meaning: garden plants with scented blooms, a noun

explanation.definitionFit: Stock is a fragrant garden flower, and stocks are shares one owns as investments.

clue.text: Plant production to rile Bert distractedly surrounded by good time girls

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the rearranged letters inside the word for good time girls

parts.note: a euphemism for prostitutes

indicators.note: distractedly means in a confused state, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A theatrical production annoys Bert, who is surrounded by party girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distractedly' scrambles RILE BERT to TLEBERRI, and 'surrounded by' sets it within the good time girls' word.
explanation.definitionFit: Whortleberries, or bilberries, are the fruit produced by a moorland shrub.

clue.text: A boy, very small

definitions.note: the definition is adjectival, describing something as tiny as the smallest particle

parts.note: Tom is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A tiny little lad.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the tiniest particle of an element, a byword for something minute.

clue.text: Mac, the gunner, in officer's 'eadgear

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
taken as written
CO is commanding officer
'at is hat with the H dropped

explanation.surface: A soldier called Mac wears his commanding officer's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Mac looks like a Scotsman's name; it is short for mackintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac, short for mackintosh, is a waterproof coat worn in rain.

clue.text: Accommodate this time only

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, this time
just means only

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to make room just this once.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to adapt, which is one sense of accommodate.

clue.text: Politicians, assessing scene prepared for the Queen, find old person sewing

indicators.note: assessing is read as being sized up inside, so the politicians sit within the scene

parts.note: a set is a scene prepared for filming or theatre
MPs are Members of Parliament
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: MPs look over a stage prepared for a royal visit and meet an old seamstress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assessing' is an unusual containment signal: the politicians sit within the prepared scene. The answer is an old form of seamster.
explanation.definitionFit: A sempster is an archaic word for a seamster, someone who sews for a living.

clue.text: Parchment unearthed from hovel — lumme!

indicators.note: unearthed from says the letters are dug out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone digs up a scroll in a shack and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Lumme is a British exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Vellum is fine parchment made from calfskin, used for manuscripts.
